## Section 5: Collateral and Guaranty

### 5.1 Security Package

Obligations of Northwind Foodservice Distribution, LLC under the Credit Agreement are secured by a first-priority security interest in all present and future Borrower assets, including accounts, inventory and deposit accounts [D2, §2.2(a)]. The Credit Agreement is dated December 15, 2022 [D2, header]. The facility totals $14.0M: a $4.0M term loan and a $10.0M revolver [D1, §3 Note to Table 3; D5, ¶2].

The Borrower leases its distribution center in Des Moines, Iowa [D2, §2.2(b)]. The center is 165,000 sq ft [D5, ¶1]. Ostrander Properties, LLC has given a landlord waiver for this location [D2, §2.2(b)].

The Borrower operates 52 delivery trucks, most under capital leases [D5, ¶1]. Fleet capital leases with Ridgeway Truck Finance were 3,420 at FY2025 [D1, §4]. Liens securing Capital Lease Obligations are Permitted Liens, limited to the leased vehicles and equipment [D2, §7.5(b)(ii)].

### 5.2 Revolver Borrowing Base

The revolver has a monthly borrowing base [D5, ¶2]. Revolving Loans may not exceed the lesser of $10,000,000 and the Borrowing Base [D2, §2.1(b)].

The Borrowing Base is (a) 85% of Eligible Accounts plus (b) the lesser of (i) 60% of Eligible Inventory at cost and (ii) $4,000,000, minus reserves the Lender may establish in its reasonable credit judgment [D2, §1.1]. Eligible Accounts are receivables not more than 60 days past the invoice date and owed by account debtors located in the United States [D2, §1.1]. Eligible Inventory has the meaning given in Schedule 1.1 [D2, §1.1].

The Borrower must deliver a Borrowing Base Certificate within 20 days after each calendar month end [D2, §7.4(d)].

Meridian revolver balances were 4,900 at FY2023, 6,600 at FY2024 and 8,100 at FY2025 [D1, §4]. Revolver availability was 3,100 at FY2023 and 2,400 at FY2024 [D1, §2: Revolver availability, FY2023 and FY2024]. FY2025 revolver availability is "Not provided" because the December 31, 2025 Borrowing Base Certificate was not in the spread export [D1, §2 Footnote *].

Excess Availability is the lesser of the Revolving Commitment and the Borrowing Base, minus Revolving Loans outstanding [D2, §1.1]. The Borrower shall not permit Excess Availability to be less than $1,000,000 at any time [D2, §7.3]. The compliance certificates do not report Excess Availability under this covenant [D1, §7].

### 5.3 Negative Pledge

The Borrower shall not create, incur or permit any Lien on its assets except Permitted Liens [D2, §7.5(a)]. Permitted Liens are: (i) Liens in favor of the Lender; (ii) Liens securing Capital Lease Obligations, limited to the leased vehicles and equipment; (iii) purchase-money Liens securing indebtedness in an aggregate amount not exceeding $500,000 at any time outstanding; and (iv) Liens for taxes not yet due and payable [D2, §7.5(b)].

### 5.4 Guaranty

Dale Ostrander has given a limited guaranty, with recourse capped at $2,000,000 in the aggregate [D2, §2.2(c)]. He holds 60% of the Borrower's membership interests [D5, ¶1]. He is 67 and plans to step back as CEO in mid-2027, with Megan Ostrander-Kolb expected to take over day-to-day operations [D5, ¶5]. Ruth Ostrander holds 20%, and Megan Ostrander-Kolb (VP Operations) holds 20% [D5, ¶1].

### 5.5 Change-of-Control Provision Linked to Guarantor

Section 7.6 provides: "It shall be an Event of Default if the members of the Borrower on the Closing Date cease to control the Borrower, or if Dale Ostrander ceases to have primary responsibility for the operations of the Borrower and a successor reasonably satisfactory to the Lender is not appointed within a reasonable period." [D2, §7.6]

The family has discussed selling up to 30% of the membership interests to an employee stock ownership plan [D5, ¶5]. There is no timeline and no engagement letter [D5, ¶5].
